chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī ʿUbaydah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If a slave runs away from his masters and then steals, his hand is not cut while he is a fugitive, because he is an apostate from Islam. Rather, he is called to return to his masters and to enter into Islam. فإذا he refuses to return to his masters, his hand is cut for the theft, then he is killed; and the apostate, if he steals, is in the same position.”

key_terms.أَبَقَ: ran away or absconded from his masters
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَتِهِ: in the same legal position or ruling
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ: his hand was cut as the theft punishment
key_terms.لَمْ يُقْطَعْ: the hadd of cutting the hand is not carried out
key_terms.مُرْتَدٌّ: one judged to have apostatized from Islam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on a fugitive slave or apostate who commits theft?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a fugitive slave who steals, treating his flight as apostasy and suspending the theft penalty until he is called back to return and re-enter Islam. If he refuses, the ruling of theft is applied to him and then the punishment of apostasy follows; the same ruling is stated for the apostate who steals.
